messages:
Acme CI: hey, our CI started failing on deploys about 10:12 UTC with 401s from the Redwood API. build logs show: 
```
POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/deploys -> 401 Unauthorized
{"error":"insufficient_scope", "message":"missing required scope: deploy:create"}
```
Acme CI: we didn't change the workflow, but our infra team did roll out token lifetime enforcement yesterday. any ideas?
Alex (support): thanks — sorry about that. quick Qs: are you still using a long-lived API key stored as a repo secret, or did you switch to OIDC?
Acme CI: still a repo secret. the secret is called REDWOOD_API_KEY and is used in multiple GH Actions jobs.
Miguel (SRE): that explains it. we pushed a policy that rejects long-lived keys without an explicit allowlist. long-lived keys now must be scoped and attached to a service account. looks like REDWOOD_API_KEY was an org-level personal key with wide scopes.
Elaine (DevEx): short-term workaround: create a short-lived service account token and drop it into the pipeline as a secret for the CI run. longer term we want OIDC.
Alex (support): to unblock right now, you can create a short TTL SA token via the Redwood Console or CLI. example CLI: 
```
rwdctl sa create --name ci-deploy --scopes inference.invoke,deploy.create --ttl 2h --output json
# returns {"token":"rwd_eyJ...","id":"sa-123"}
```
Alex (support): but please avoid using deploy.create if you only need to call inference endpoints. principle of least privilege: only add the scopes actually needed (inference.invoke, models.list).
Acme CI: ok we can do that. how do we migrate to OIDC so we don't bake secrets?
Miguel (SRE): for GitHub Actions use the OIDC flow. sample step: 
```yaml
- name: Request OIDC token
  id: oidc
  uses: actions/checkout@v4
- name: Exchange OIDC for Redwood token
  run: |
    OIDC_TOKEN=$(curl -s -X POST -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" \
      \"https://api.redwood.ai/v1/oidc/exchange\" \
      -d '{"id_token":"'$GITHUB_TOKEN'","audience":"redwood-ci"}')
    echo "RWD_TOKEN=$OIDC_TOKEN" >> $GITHUB_ENV
```
Miguel (SRE): in the Console you'll register GitHub as an identity provider and set allowed audience to `redwood-ci`. then create a service account that trusts that provider and only issues tokens when the aud claim matches.
Elaine (DevEx): config snippet for the SA policy (Console -> Service Accounts -> Advanced -> JSON policy): 
```json
{"name":"ci-deploy","trusted_idps":[{"provider":"github","aud":"redwood-ci","repos":["acme/*"]}],"scopes":["inference.invoke","models.list"],"max_ttl_seconds":21600}
```
Alex (support): couple of gotchas we've seen:
- if you previously used an account with wildcard scopes (admin), the new enforcement will reject it. check your audit logs (Console -> Activity) for `token.issued` failures.
- some GH Actions runners pass a different audience by default; confirm the ID token contains `aud: \"redwood-ci\"`.
- ensure CI uses the exchanged token as an Authorization: Bearer <token>, not the raw ID token.
Acme CI: we tried the OIDC exchange and got `400 invalid_audience` when calling /v1/oidc/exchange.
Miguel (SRE): that means the ID token aud doesn't match. quick debug: print the ID token in the job (masking secrets) and decode at jwt.io or use `jq -Rr '@base64'` trick. on GH, you need `permissions: id-token: write` and `with: audience: redwood-ci` in `actions/github-script` or when requesting the token.
Elaine (DevEx): example GH Action to get ID token directly: 
```yaml
- name: Get ID token
  id: id-token
  uses: actions/github-script@v6
  with:
    script: |
      const id = await github.actions.getOIDCToken({audience: 'redwood-ci'})
      console.log(id.token)
```
Miguel (SRE): final security recommendations:
- create dedicated SA per repo/team, each with minimal scopes.
- set max_ttl_seconds to something reasonable (1-6 hours).
- enable audit logging and set alerts for `token.issued` failures and `auth.denied` spikes.
Alex (support): I've opened internal ticket RWD-6789 and set priority = high. support-bot: created a customer incident and attached the logs.
support-bot: INCIDENT RWD-6789 created, linked to acme-ci support thread, priority: high :rotating_light:
Acme CI: thanks all — creating a ci-deploy SA now with inference.invoke and models.list, will test and report back.
Miguel (SRE): if you want, post the `rwdctl sa create` output here and we'll sanity-check the policy. also after you migrate, rotate and delete the old REDWOOD_API_KEY.
Alex (support): follow-up checklist for us: (1) help them migrate to OIDC, (2) review SA scopes and reduce to least privilege, (3) verify tokens issued include correct `aud`, (4) ensure pipeline uses Bearer header with exchanged token.
Acme CI: noted. pinging if we hit any more errors. :thumbsup:
